purpose: Scope and boundary record for one reading of the fixed native TeX. Describes what the author assumes/asserts and where; it does not certify correctness and does not repair notation.

necessary_conditions_by_object.conditions: Base is T*T^n with n>=1 (torus, not R^n); H in C^infty_c(R/Z x T*T^n,R), 1-periodic in t, compactly supported in (q,p); H_k(t,q,p)=H(kt,kq,p). Non-compact and time-dependent variants are separate results (Section 11), not part of Theorem 3.1's hypothesis.

Convergence is in the metric gamma on DHam_c(T*T^n)/Ham_c defined by minimax critical values of GFQI (Section 2, Definitions 2.1-2.9), i.e. c(mu)-c(1); completions gclDHam_c, gclHam_c (Humiliere). The author stresses at 165-168 that this implies NO pointwise or a.e. convergence of flows or Hamiltonians. C^0 convergence of flows DOES imply gamma-convergence (citation at 166-168, 2808); the converse implication (gamma-convergence of flows gives convergence of Hamiltonians) is explicitly NOT known in general (footnote at 790).

c(alpha,S)=inf{lambda : image of T⊗alpha in H^*(S^lambda,S^{-infty}) is nonzero}, for NONZERO alpha only; 1 is the generator of H^0(M), mu the generator of H^n(M); gamma(L)=c(mu,S)-c(1,S). Minimax over cohomology; the homology variant is defined separately in Remark 2.4(4) with a different formula (inf over lambda such that the image of T⊗u lies in the image of H_*(S^lambda,S^{-infty})).

c(alpha,S) depends on L only up to a global shift; fixing the shift requires normalising S (Remark 2.4(2)), for T^n-type graphs the normalisation is by the compactified graph overline Gamma(phi) with critical value zero at the fixed point at infinity. Consequently c(alpha,(Lambda)_y) is well-defined only up to a constant independent of y, and differences c(beta,(Lambda)_y)-c(alpha,(Lambda)_y) depend on the global Lambda, not only on its reduction (Remark 4.9(1)).

necessary_conditions_by_object.object: the homogenised limit and its quantifiers
necessary_conditions_by_object.conditions: Hbar in C^0_c(R^n,R); the defining formula in the autonomous case is Hbar(p)=lim_k c(mu⊗1(p),H_k) (Remark 3.3(1), line 597), the limit being as the INTEGER k tends to infinity, uniformly in p (used at 1192-1196). Existence of the limit is proved, not assumed (4.6 + 4.12 + 4.14). The construction is by subsequence (Proposition 4.15 holds along a sequence k_nu) and upgraded to the whole sequence via 4.12.

H(t,x,y,q,p) compactly supported on T*T^{n+m}; the statement is for all variables x homogeneous of degree one in the scaling (kt,kx) with t also rescaled. Only M=T^*T^m is proved; the general symplectic M case is declared adaptable (line 628). The effective Hamiltonian is Hbar(y,q,p), a function of the FROZEN variables; the flow formula in Remark 3.6(2) is given only in case Hbar is smooth (line 664).

Variational solutions (not viscosity solutions) of HJ_k and HJbar, with H in C^0([0,1] x T*T^{n+m}) either coercive or compactly supported and f in C^0; the conclusion is UNIFORM on compact time intervals and of the form |u_k-u|<=eps_k t for t>=1 (Proposition 3.7). For the coercive non-autonomous case the solution concept and the operator Hbar change (Definition 11.9, lower semi-continuous limit) and the conclusion is only uniform on bounded time intervals.

Uses the suspension K(t,tau,q,p)=tau+H(t,q,p) on T*(T^{n+1}), truncated K_A=chi_A(K)K; K_A is compactly supported and autonomous. The identity Kbar(tau,p)=tau+Hbar(p) is proved only on the region |tau|<=A-||H|| (line 2426) and then extended. The transfer of properties is restricted at line 2500 to (1),(2),(3),(6) of Theorem 3.2.

Autonomous: lim_{|p|->infty}H(q,p)=+infty, no convexity needed for existence; convexity of Hbar is claimed only for H convex in p, via the CIPP inf-sup formula, hence only after the Tonelli identification 12.4. Non-autonomous coercive: Hbar is defined by a limsup over compactly supported K<=H; only well-definedness and lower semi-continuity are asserted, and continuity is explicitly OPEN (2522-2525). The non-coercive example requires H(x1,x2,p1,p2)=h(p) outside a compact set.

L is C^2, strictly convex with d^2L/dxi^2>eps Id, coercive, complete Euler-Lagrange flow (Tonelli, Definition 12.3); H is its Legendre dual, strictly convex in p. Mather's alpha is taken with free endpoints and C^1 paths. The identification is Hbar(p)=alpha(p); the symplectic invariance is attributed to Bernard and only the torus case is re-derived.

H(q,kp) has NO gamma-limit in general (author notes at 2640 and 2661 that Hbar(kp) has no limit); the statement 12.1 is that gamma(H(q,kp),Hbar(kp))->0. The map zeta_k(q,p)=(q,kp) is a bona fide map on T*T^n (no covering argument), whereas rho_k(q,p)=(kq,p) is not invertible and needs the lift to T*R^n with Z^n-equivariance (Section 4, 805-811; Remark 4.2).

H(x,y,p) compactly supported but K(x,y,p_x,p_y)=H(x,y,p_x+p_y) is not compactly supported and only C^2 bounded; the reduction to the compactly supported theory is ASSERTED at 3221-3223 ('this is enough to carry on symplectic homogenization as in Sections 6-8'), not proved.

quantifier_and_limit_details_to_preserve: Sequence vs subsequence: 4.15 is stated and proved only for a sequence (k_nu) going to infinity; the passage to all k is via 4.12 plus the metric-space argument in footnote 1105 (every subsequence has a sub-subsequence with the same limit).

Iteration index is an INTEGER k in H_k(t,q,p)=H(kt,kq,p); intermediate real powers phi^{1/r} are used only through the fixed integer r trick at 834-849, and c scaling in 3.2(3) treats c integer, c=1/q, then c<0 separately.
The limit is k->+infty, and the error in Proposition 3.7 is eps_k t with eps_k = sup_{t in [0,1]} gamma(phi_k^t phibar^{-t}) (2345-2347), i.e. grows linearly in t and is not uniform in t.
Convergence of ell_k(alpha,beta) in 13.2 is over k integer and the second equality ellbar(alpha,beta)=ellbar(alpha) uses flatness of the limit Finsler metric, not of the approximating g_k.
In 12.1 and 12.2 the limit is k->infty inside gamma resp. t->infty for (1/t)u(t,q); the two limits are not interchangeable and are not claimed to be.

In 11.10 the definition is a limsup over the directed set {K in C^0_c : K<=H} AND a lim_{r->infty} of overline{f_r(H)} simultaneously displayed (line 2508); it is not a plain limit of the H_k sequence.

The sigma_k smallness condition (star) in Section 9 (2247-2251) is a condition inside the proof, quantified as 'for k large enough' with l fixed first (footnote 2262: 'in our case l is fixed and k can be taken arbitrarily large'); the order of quantifiers l then k matters.
The truncation parameter A in Section 11 tends to +infty AFTER the homogenisation of each K_A; line 2466 also allows H equal to a constant c outside a compact set with Hbar=c+overline{(H-c)}.
core_recount_boundaries: T*T^n vs T*R^n: the main construction uses rho_k(q,p)=(kq,p) which is not invertible on T*T^n; all generating-function identities are lifted to T*R^n and descended via Z^n-equivariance (805-811, 851-854). Appendix D separately uses W={(q1,q2)}/Z^n acting diagonally. Do not identify these two quotients.

Spatial vs temporal periodicity: H is 1-periodic in t and the rescaling kt is applied to time simultaneously with kq in space (Theorem 3.1). Homogenising time alone is Section 13.1 and gives the time average; homogenising only some variables is Theorem 3.5. The three scalings H(kt,kq,p), H(kt,kx,y,q,p) and H(q,kp) have different limits and are not instances of each other.

Partial vs full homogenisation: full homogenisation yields a function of p only and a projector A with A^2=A; partial homogenisation yields Hbar(y,q,p) and A_x, and Remark 3.6(3) states that Hbar need NOT depend only on the time-one map, in contrast with 3.1(2).

Autonomous vs non-autonomous: Theorem 3.1 is first proved for autonomous compactly supported H (Sections 4-8) and only then extended; the extension is not a corollary of a formal argument but of the suspension construction, and the property transfer is limited at line 2500.

Hamiltonian vs time-one map: 3.1(2) asserts dependence only on phi^1 for the full homogenisation (using Corollary A.2); the gamma-convergence statement 3.1(1) is about the Hamiltonians, and the author remarks at 790-791 that in the completion the exponential map need not be injective, resolving it only through A.2.

Smooth vs continuous vs C^0-bounded: the core theorem is C^infty_c; coercive C^0 Hamiltonians are handled by truncation with only lower semi-continuity of Hbar (11.10); Appendix C uses a merely C^2-bounded non-proper Hamiltonian with the enabling claim flagged above. Characteristic functions of open sets are NOT elements of gclHam_c (Remark 3.3(3)), and A is extended to them by a decreasing-sequence construction, with the author explicitly saying the properties may fail.

Support conditions: compact support / fixed support is used repeatedly (e.g. fixed compact support in 11.2 and in the definition of the completion); fiber support and finite propagation are NOT assumed and must not be added. Tonelli (coercive + complete flow) is imposed only in Section 12/Appendix D, and convexity only there and in 11.4/11.10.

gamma vs Hofer vs C^0 vs C^1: gamma is a spectral (minimax) metric; C^0 convergence of Hamiltonians with fixed support implies gamma (2.10); C^1 closeness of Hamiltonians/flows is used only as a technical genericity or composition hypothesis (e.g. 856-859, 2247). gamma-convergence is NOT replaced anywhere by pointwise convergence of Hamiltonians, and the author constructs an explicit discontinuous example (Section 13.3) where Hbar is discontinuous.

gamma convergence is explicitly compared to Gamma-convergence of De Giorgi but not identified with it (166-172); the variational-solution convergence in 3.7 is not viscosity-solution convergence, except via the cited convex case (699-700).

The p-homogenisation uses tau_k which is not Hamiltonian (footnote 2648): gamma-invariance under tau_k is recovered by lifting and by equality of action spectra, so do not treat tau_k as a Hamiltonian conjugation.

Mather alpha, Legendre duality and the inf-sup formula apply only under the stated Tonelli/strict convexity assumptions; the paper does not extend Hbar=alpha to non-convex H (and says so, citing [NCMT] at 191 for the non-convex programme).
